```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE,
                      fig.width = 8, fig.height = 4.2, dpi = 120, dev = "png",
                      fig.path = "figures/")
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(readr); library(dplyr); library(tidyr); library(ggplot2); library(scales); library(knitr)
})
tb <- function(name) read_tsv(file.path(params$tables, name), show_col_types = FALSE)

acc   <- tb("accuracy.tsv")
conc  <- tb("concordance.tsv")
titr  <- tb("titration.tsv")
crit  <- tb("acceptance.tsv")
samp  <- tb("samples.tsv")
disc  <- tb("discordance.tsv")
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 12) + theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))
pal <- c(SNV = "#2c7fb8", INDEL = "#d95f0e")
pct <- function(x, d = 2) ifelse(is.na(x), "", sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x))
```

## 1. Summary

```{r verdict}
failed  <- crit$criterion[crit$result == "FAIL"]
overall <- if (length(failed) == 0) "meets all" else
  sprintf("meets %d of %d", sum(crit$result == "PASS"), sum(crit$result %in% c("PASS", "FAIL")))
```

The pipeline **`r overall`** pre-defined acceptance criteria`r if (length(failed)) paste0(". Not met: ", paste(failed, collapse = "; "), ". See section 6 for the investigation and corrective action") else ""`. All samples are reference material
from the Genome in a Bottle consortium, sequenced on Illumina HiSeq 2500 (2 x 148 bp) and benchmarked against the
GIAB v4.2.1 truth sets inside GIAB high-confidence regions that overlap the panel.

```{r acceptance}
crit %>%
  mutate(observed = ifelse(grepl("^[0-9.]+$", observed) & suppressWarnings(as.numeric(observed)) <= 1,
                           pct(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(observed)), 4), paste0(observed, "x")),
         threshold = ifelse(grepl("^[0-9.]+$", threshold), pct(suppressWarnings(as.numeric(threshold)), 2), threshold)) %>%
  select(Criterion = criterion, Observed = observed, `Acceptance` = threshold, Result = result, Detail = detail) %>%
  kable()
```

## 2. Study design

| Study | Question answered | Samples |
|---|---|---|
| Accuracy | Does the assay call the right variants? | every HG001 run at 30x + HG002 at 30x |
| Repeatability | Same library, same instrument, short time window: do replicates agree? | 3 disjoint read subsets |
| Reproducibility | Different sequencing runs, instruments and dates (Dec 2013 to Apr 2014) | 4 independent runs |
| Depth titration | Lowest depth at which SNV sensitivity stays above target (limit of detection) | 5x to 100x |

```{r samples}
samp %>%
  mutate(pct_target_20x = pct(pct_target_20x, 1)) %>%
  select(Sample = sample, Study = study, Material = reference_material, Source = source,
         `Nominal depth` = nominal_depth, `Observed depth` = observed_depth,
         `Target >= 20x` = pct_target_20x, QC = qc_status) %>%
  kable()
```

## 3. Accuracy

Sensitivity = TP / (TP + FN), PPV = TP / (TP + FP), both with 95% Wilson score intervals.
Genotype must match for a call to count as a true positive (RTG vcfeval, haplotype-aware comparison).

```{r accuracy-table}
acc_typed <- acc %>% filter(type != "ALL") %>% left_join(samp %>% select(sample, study), by = "sample")
acc_typed %>%
  filter(study %in% c("accuracy", "repeatability", "reproducibility")) %>%
  transmute(Sample = sample, Type = type, TP = tp, FP = fp, FN = fn,
            Sensitivity = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(sensitivity), pct(sens_lo), pct(sens_hi)),
            PPV = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(ppv), pct(ppv_lo), pct(ppv_hi)),
            F1 = sprintf("%.4f", f1)) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r accuracy-plot, fig.height = 4.6}
acc_typed %>%
  filter(study %in% c("accuracy", "repeatability", "reproducibility")) %>%
  select(sample, type, sensitivity, sens_lo, sens_hi, ppv, ppv_lo, ppv_hi) %>%
  pivot_longer(c(sensitivity, ppv), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
  mutate(lo = ifelse(metric == "sensitivity", sens_lo, ppv_lo),
         hi = ifelse(metric == "sensitivity", sens_hi, ppv_hi),
         metric = recode(metric, sensitivity = "Sensitivity", ppv = "PPV")) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = value, y = sample, colour = type)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = lo, xmax = hi), height = 0.25, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  geom_point(size = 2.2, position = position_dodge(width = 0.5)) +
  facet_wrap(~metric) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1), breaks = c(0.94, 0.96, 0.98, 1)) +
  theme(panel.spacing.x = unit(1.5, "lines")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL, title = "Per-run accuracy with 95% confidence intervals")
```

### Specificity

Specificity is reported per base: every high-confidence reference position that is not a truth variant counts as a
negative, and any PASS call there is a false positive. Because nearly all positions are reference, this figure is
always very close to 100%. PPV is the more informative measure of false-positive burden, so both are reported.

```{r specificity}
acc %>% filter(type == "ALL") %>%
  transmute(Sample = sample, `Bases evaluated` = comma(eval_bp), `True negatives` = comma(tn), FP = fp,
            Specificity = sprintf("%.5f%% (%.5f-%.5f)", 100 * specificity, 100 * spec_lo, 100 * spec_hi)) %>%
  kable()
```

## 4. Precision: repeatability and reproducibility

Concordance = calls with identical genotype in both replicates / all distinct calls in either replicate
(PASS calls inside the evaluation region).

```{r concordance}
conc %>%
  transmute(Study = study, `Replicate A` = sample_a, `Replicate B` = sample_b, Shared = shared,
            `Only A` = only_a, `Only B` = only_b, `GT match` = genotype_match,
            Concordance = sprintf("%s (%s-%s)", pct(concordance), pct(conc_lo), pct(conc_hi))) %>%
  kable()
```

```{r concordance-plot, fig.height = 3.6}
conc %>%
  mutate(pair = paste(sub("HG001_", "", sample_a), "vs", sub("HG001_", "", sample_b))) %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = concordance, y = reorder(pair, concordance), colour = study)) +
  geom_errorbarh(aes(xmin = conc_lo, xmax = conc_hi), height = 0.25) +
  geom_point(size = 2.4) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(repeatability = "#41ab5d", reproducibility = "#807dba")) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 0.1)) +
  labs(x = "Pairwise genotype concordance", y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

### Discordant calls

```{r discordance}
disc %>%
  transmute(Study = study, Calls = calls, N = n, `Median depth` = median_dp,
            `Depth < 15` = pct(frac_dp_lt15, 1), `Depth < 20` = pct(frac_dp_lt20, 1),
            `GQ < 20` = pct(frac_gq_lt20, 1)) %>%
  kable()
```

## 5. Depth titration (limit of detection)

```{r titration-plot, fig.height = 4}
ggplot(titr, aes(x = nominal_depth, y = sensitivity, colour = type)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(0.99, 0.95), linetype = "dashed", colour = "grey60") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) + geom_point(size = 2.2) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = pal) +
  scale_x_continuous(trans = "log2", breaks = sort(unique(titr$nominal_depth))) +
  scale_y_continuous(labels = percent_format(accuracy = 1)) +
  labs(x = "Mean depth (x, log2 scale)", y = "Sensitivity", colour = NULL,
       title = "Sensitivity vs sequencing depth (HG001)")
```

```{r titration-table}
titr %>%
  select(type, nominal_depth, observed_depth, sensitivity, ppv) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = type, values_from = c(sensitivity, ppv)) %>%
  transmute(`Nominal depth` = nominal_depth, `Observed depth` = observed_depth,
            `SNV sens` = pct(sensitivity_SNV), `SNV PPV` = pct(ppv_SNV),
            `Indel sens` = pct(sensitivity_INDEL), `Indel PPV` = pct(ppv_INDEL)) %>%
  kable()
```

## 6. Findings and corrective action

```{r findings}
rep_min  <- min(conc$concordance[conc$study == "repeatability"])
d_disc   <- disc$frac_dp_lt15[disc$study == "repeatability" & disc$calls == "discordant"]
d_conc   <- disc$frac_dp_lt15[disc$study == "repeatability" & disc$calls == "concordant"]
qc30     <- samp %>% filter(study %in% c("repeatability", "reproducibility", "accuracy"))
gate     <- samp %>% filter(study == "titration") %>% arrange(nominal_depth) %>%
              filter(pct_target_20x >= 0.95) %>% slice(1)
snv_lod  <- crit$observed[grepl("^Minimum depth", crit$criterion)]
```

**Finding 1: repeatability below target.** The lowest pairwise concordance between same-batch replicates was
`r pct(rep_min)` against a target of 99%. Discordant calls are enriched for low read depth:
`r pct(d_disc, 0)` of discordant calls have fewer than 15 reads, compared with `r pct(d_conc, 0)` of concordant calls.
This points to random sampling of reads at ~30x rather than a systematic pipeline fault (the same replicates
reach `r pct(min(acc$sensitivity[acc$type == "SNV" & acc$sample %in% qc30$sample]))` or better SNV sensitivity).

**Finding 2: the 30x replicates do not meet the per-sample coverage gate.** Only
`r pct(min(qc30$pct_target_20x), 1)` to `r pct(max(qc30$pct_target_20x), 1)` of target bases reach 20x,
below the 95% requirement. In the titration series the gate is first met at
`r gate$nominal_depth`x nominal depth (`r gate$observed_depth`x observed). SNV sensitivity reaches 99% from
`r snv_lod`x.

**Corrective action.** The acceptance criteria are not changed after the fact. Instead:

1. Minimum sequencing depth for the assay is set to **`r round(gate$nominal_depth)`x mean target depth**, the lowest
   level at which both the coverage gate and the sensitivity target are met.
2. Repeatability and reproducibility must be repeated with replicates at that depth before the assay is released.
   The GIAB data used here supports at most ~34x per same-batch replicate on this panel, so this needs new
   sequencing of the reference material.
3. Until then, calls with depth < 15 or GQ < 20 are flagged for manual review (query 6 in `sql/queries.sql`).

## 7. Limitations

* The panel covers 1.5 Mb of chr20, so indel counts are small and their confidence intervals are wide.
  A clinical validation would add more loci and more reference samples (for example HG003 to HG007) to reach the
  sample sizes in the validation plan.
* Repeatability and reproducibility replicates are read subsets from GIAB sequencing runs rather than separate
  library preparations, so they capture sequencing and analysis variation but not wet-lab variation.
* Only regions that GIAB marks as high-confidence are scored. Difficult regions (segmental duplications,
  long homopolymers) are outside the benchmark and need separate handling, for example with orthogonal confirmation.
* Copy-number variants, structural variants and mosaic variants are out of scope.
